newsitem.title: USA: Case, Pioneer, Dow form farm info venture.
newsitem.headline: Case, Pioneer, Dow form farm info venture.

text.p: Case Corp, Dow Chemical Co's DowElanco unit, and Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc said Monday they had agreed to collaborate in a venture aimed at managing farming information.

The companies said they will focus on "learning and determining how the interactions of various farming practices, inputs and environmental conditions can be collected, processed and turned into information to help farmers make better crop production decisions."
Financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.
The firms said they will decide sometime in the next two years on "the practicality of offering management information gained from the study to farmers on a wide-area basis."
The agreement does not preclude any of the companies from entering into collaborative agreements with other companies in the future, they said.

"The companies will partner to study better ways to plan, plant, manage and harvest corn and soybean in the Corn Belt. Farmers have been identified who will supply land for the project," the companies said.
Various soils and maturity zones in the Central Corn Belt will be represented in the study, the companies said.
"Our plan is to test seed, chemicals, fertilizers, tillage, planting and a host of other corn management practices, under actual conditions, on several working farms," they said.

"Many decisions made by farmers are based on a combination of instinct and past experience. We hope to uncover some predictable patterns in managing a crop that will give farmers better information on which to base their decisions, from planning to marketing a crop," they said.
